commands.name: agent-reach
commands.description:
MUST USE when user wants to 调研/research/搜索/search/查/找/look up anything on the internet — e.g. 全网调研 X / 帮我调研一下 X / 查一下 X / 搜搜 X / 看看大家怎么评价 X / X 上有什么讨论 / research this topic。
Also MUST USE when user mentions any platform or shares any URL/链接: 小红书/xiaohongshu/xhs, Twitter/推特/X, B站/bilibili, Reddit, Facebook, Instagram, V2EX, LinkedIn/领英/招聘/求职/jobs, YouTube, GitHub code search, 小宇宙播客, 雪球/股票行情, RSS feeds, or any web URL.
15 platforms, multi-backend routing (OpenCLI / per-platform CLIs / APIs). Zero config for 6 channels. Run `agent-reach doctor --json` to see which backend serves each platform right now.
NOT for: 写报告/数据分析/翻译等内容加工（本 skill 只负责从互联网获取内容）； 发帖/评论/点赞等写操作；已有专门 skill 的平台（先用专门 skill）。
【路由方式】SKILL.md 包含路由表和常用命令，复杂场景需按需阅读对应分类的 references/*.md。 分类：search / social (小红书/推特/B站/V2EX/Reddit/Facebook/Instagram) / career(LinkedIn) / dev(github) / web(网页/文章/RSS) / video(YouTube/B站/播客)。 (user)

commands.name: docx
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation. (user)

commands.name: mcp-builder
commands.description: Guide for creating high-quality MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers that enable LLMs to interact with external services through well-designed tools. Use when building MCP servers to integrate external APIs or services, whether in Python (FastMCP) or Node/TypeScript (MCP SDK). (user)

commands.name: morning
commands.description: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead. (user)

commands.name: pdf
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill. (user)

commands.name: pptx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill. (user)

commands.name: startup-hook-skill
commands.description: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions. (user)

commands.name: skill-creator
commands.description: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy. (user)

commands.name: ui-ux-pro-max
commands.description: UI/UX design intelligence for web and mobile. Searchable local database with 84 styles, 192 color palettes, 74 font pairings, 192 product types, 98 UX guidelines, 104 icon entries, 16 GSAP motion presets, and 25 chart types across 22 stacks (React, Next.js, Vue, Nuxt, Svelte, Astro, SwiftUI, React Native, Flutter, Tailwind, shadcn/ui, Jetpack Compose, Angular, Laravel, JavaFX, WPF, WinUI, Avalonia, Uno Platform, UWP, Three.js, and HTML/CSS). Use when designing, building, or reviewing UI: pages, components, color schemes, typography, layout, accessibility, animation, or data visualization. (user)

commands.name: web-artifacts-builder
commands.description: Suite of tools for creating elaborate, multi-component claude.ai HTML artifacts using modern frontend web technologies (React, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui). Use for complex artifacts requiring state management, routing, or shadcn/ui components - not for simple single-file HTML/JSX artifacts. (user)

commands.name: xlsx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved. (user)

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: artifact-design
commands.description: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.

commands.name: artifact-diagramming
commands.description: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.

commands.name: artifact-capabilities
commands.description: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Build OS — routing-gate.sh: the LIVE dispatch gate (PACKET-0053-live-enforcement).
3	#
4	# WHAT THIS IS. Claude Code PreToolUse hooks receive the pending tool call as
5	# JSON on stdin and can BLOCK it: exit 2 makes stderr the model-visible refusal.
6	# That converts routing from file-instruction (PACKET-0050's close-time gate,
7	# which refuses AFTER the tokens are spent) into pre-execution enforcement for
8	# everything dispatch-shaped. EXP-0003 measured the gap this closes: both
9	# condition receipts were REFUSED at close and ZERO degradation notes were
10	# written mid-flight, because nothing mechanical existed mid-flight.
11	#
12	# PACKET-0054 EXTENDED THIS FILE (never forked it) into the UNIVERSAL TASK-ENTRY
13	# boundary: the gate now also fires on MUTATION-CAPABLE tools (Edit, Write,
14	# NotebookEdit, Bash) via the `mutgate` subcommand, so parent-only work that
15	# dispatches nothing is governed too. Contract half:
16	# build-os/memory/routing_contract_live.md; adapter expression:
17	# build-os/memory/provider_adapter_contract.md (this file is ADAPTER #1).
18	#
19	# SUBCOMMANDS (wired in .claude/settings.json):
20	#   gate    PreToolUse, matcher Task|Agent — the dispatch gate. BLOCKS (exit 2):
21	#             * when NO open routing receipt exists (open = newest receipt in
22	#               build-os/packets/routing/ whose executed_mode is '-');
23	#             * when the open receipt records direct/gravito_light and carries
24	#               no evidence-bearing escalation record (silent escalation,
25	#               refused BEFORE execution — routing-check.sh's own escalation
26	#               semantics, reused not re-invented);
27	#             * when the receipt is DEGRADED (degradation_note filled);
28	#             * when task dispatches have reached budget_max_subagents (the
29	#               live fan-out brake — fires BEFORE close, stamps the degradation
30	#               via record-degradation.sh, and instructs consolidate-and-
31	#               continue, never stop-working);
32	#             * when process-role dispatches (subagent_type builder|qa|
33	#               reviewer|archivist|build-orchestrator) have reached
34	#               process_dispatch_allowance (default 4 where the receipt
35	#               predates the field) — attributed to governance_process,
36	#               SEPARATE from the task budget. This resolves the PACKET-0050/
37	#               0051 open calibration question mechanically: a packet's own
38	#               gate chain does not eat its task budget.
39	#           On ALLOW it appends the dispatch to the live state and, for Full
40	#           task dispatches, seeds a stub contribution row into the receipt
41	#           (close-fill tooling for the marginal-contribution table).
42	#   mutgate PreToolUse, matcher Edit|Write|NotebookEdit|Bash — the TASK-ENTRY
43	#           gate (PACKET-0054). A mutation-capable call with NO open routing
44	#           receipt is BLOCKED with the recovery command (route-task.sh, incl a
45	#           cheap direct-mode example — tiny work routes too, cheaply). Two
46	#           classes pass UNGATED, logged: (a) DEADLOCK GUARD — since
47	#           PACKET-0055 a STRUCTURED ROUTING ACTION: only a command whose
48	#           extracted tool_input.command field IS exactly one clean routing-
49	#           tool invocation (no chaining/substitution metacharacters) passes,
50	#           logged ROUTING-TOOL-PASS with an action fingerprint (tool, sha256,
51	#           excerpt); everything else falls through TOWARD GATING. (b) READ-
52	#           ONLY git inspection (status/log/diff/show/rev-parse/ls-files/
53	#           branch), counted exploratory. Any git command carrying push|commit|
54	#           merge|rebase|reset|checkout|restore|clean|apply|am|cherry-pick|tag|
55	#           stash or -f/--force is mutation-capable. The classification is a
56	#           NAMED HEURISTIC (sh -c evades the mutation class): discipline-for-
57	#           honest-agents plus audit trail, NOT a sandbox (the sandbox is the
58	#           platform's permission system). Fire-once REASSESS trip (see count).
59	#   count   PreToolUse, matcher * — the tool-event counter. NEVER blocks.
60	#           Deliberately jq-free (sed only) so its per-call overhead stays
61	#           trivial; the suite measures and asserts the bound. PACKET-0054:
62	#           each row carries chars= (the ESTIMATE token-proxy input); Read/
63	#           Grep/Glob additionally append an exploratory_event row (the
64	#           explore half of the explore/execute split); and the counter ARMS
65	#           the repetitive-loop trip — consecutive same-tool calls >=
66	#           ROUTING_REASSESS_SAME_TOOL_MAX (derived default 25) or chars/4 >=
67	#           ROUTING_REASSESS_PROXY_MULT (default 4) x
68	#           budget_max_uncached_tokens — which blocks the NEXT mutation-capable
69	#           call ONCE with a REASSESS refusal; a reassessment record (fresh
70	#           receipt, or an escalation/degradation entry) resets the trip.
71	#   post    PostToolUse, matcher * — counts a tool_failure ONLY where the
72	#           tool_response exposes success:false / is_error:true. Where no
73	#           status is exposed, nothing is guessed — the state-file label
74	#           admits the bound.
75	#   status  Human/test convenience: derived counts + elapsed_s for the open
76	#           receipt. Counts are DERIVED by counting append-only rows, never
77	#           stored — a stored counter is a second copy that can disagree.
78	#
79	# WHEN THIS GOES LIVE. Hooks load at SESSION START: the session that wires this
80	# file is NOT governed by it; every later session in this project is. Stated in
81	# build-os/memory/routing_contract_live.md, not implied.
82	#
83	# FAIL-OPEN, BY DESIGN. On any internal error (unparseable stdin, unreadable
84	# store, missing dependency) the gate ALLOWS and logs a FAIL-OPEN row: a gate
85	# that fails closed on its own bug is a denial of service against the operator.
86	# ROUTING_GATE_DISABLE=1 is the documented OPERATOR-ONLY escape; it admits the
87	# call and logs DISABLED-BY-OPERATOR — an escape that leaves no trace is a
88	# bypass, so the trace is not optional.
89	#
90	# WRITES (censused: MUT-0011, control routing.live_gate_ledger_append):
91	#   append-only build-os/packets/routing/live_gate_log.tsv     (every decision)
92	#   append-only build-os/packets/routing/live_state/<id>.tsv   (per open receipt)
93	#   append-only stub contribution rows into the open receipt   (ALLOW, Full task)
94	# ROUTING_GATE_ROOT overrides the DATA root (fixtures); code always resolves
95	# beside this file. Reads receipts; never edits a receipt field itself — the
96	# degradation stamp is build-os/tools/record-degradation.sh's, invoked here.
97	set -uo pipefail
98	
99	SELF_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
100	CODE_ROOT="$(cd "$SELF_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
101	DATA_ROOT="${ROUTING_GATE_ROOT:-${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$CODE_ROOT}}"
102	RDIR="$DATA_ROOT/build-os/packets/routing"
103	LOGF="$RDIR/live_gate_log.tsv"
104	SDIR="$RDIR/live_state"
105	RECDEG="$CODE_ROOT/build-os/tools/record-degradation.sh"
106	PROCESS_ROLES="builder qa reviewer archivist build-orchestrator"
107	DEFAULT_PROCESS_ALLOWANCE=7
108	# Reassessment-trip thresholds: DERIVED DEFAULTS, operator-tunable via env —
109	# stated as such in every refusal; neither is a law.
110	SAME_TOOL_MAX="${ROUTING_REASSESS_SAME_TOOL_MAX:-25}"
111	PROXY_MULT="${ROUTING_REASSESS_PROXY_MULT:-4}"
112	
113	now(){ date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ; }
114	
115	# Append one decision row: timestamp, task identity, selected depth, decision, detail.
116	# Best-effort on purpose: logging must never turn a decision into a crash.
117	logrow(){ # <task_id> <depth> <decision> <detail>
118	  # Best-effort log append; when the routing store is unwritable the row goes
119	  # to STDERR instead, so the trace survives the one vector that silences the
120	  # file (named in routing_contract_live.md layer 4). Never fails the caller.
121	  if ! { mkdir -p "$RDIR" 2>/dev/null && \
122	    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$(now)" "${1:--}" "${2:--}" "${3:--}" "${4:--}" >> "$LOGF"; } 2>/dev/null; then
123	    { printf 'routing-gate UNLOGGED(store unwritable): %s %s %s %s\n' "${1:--}" "${2:--}" "${3:--}" "${4:--}" >&9; } 2>/dev/null || printf 'routing-gate UNLOGGED(store unwritable): %s %s %s %s\n' "${1:--}" "${2:--}" "${3:--}" "${4:--}" >&2 || true
124	  fi
125	}
126	
127	# The ONE label block, shared verbatim with record-degradation.sh (the suite
128	# diffs the two writers' label blocks so they cannot drift apart). EXACT vs
129	# ESTIMATE is labeled per field — the operator's rule, in the artefact itself.
130	write_labels(){ # <dest-file> <receipt-basename> — create-once via noclobber
131	  ( set -C; { \
132	    printf '# live state for %s — append-only; counts are DERIVED by counting rows, never stored\n' "$2"; \
133	    printf 'label\ttask_dispatches\tEXACT (hook-counted ALLOW decisions at PreToolUse, in sessions where the gate is loaded; attempts, not completions)\n'; \
134	    printf 'label\tprocess_dispatches\tEXACT (hook-counted; subagent_type in builder|qa|reviewer|archivist|build-orchestrator; attributed governance_process)\n'; \
135	    printf 'label\ttool_events\tEXACT (hook-counted PreToolUse events in sessions where the gate is loaded)\n'; \
136	    printf 'label\ttool_failures\tEXACT only where PostToolUse exposes success:false/is_error; otherwise unavailable — absence of a row is NOT evidence of success\n'; \
137	    printf 'label\texploratory_events\tEXACT (hook-counted Read/Grep/Glob and read-only git inspection — the explore half of the explore/execute split)\n'; \
138	    printf 'label\tmutation_events\tEXACT (hook-counted ADMITTED mutation-capable calls: Edit/Write/NotebookEdit/Bash outside the routing-tool and read-only-git classes)\n'; \
139	    printf 'label\ttoken_proxy\tESTIMATE (sum of tool-input chars / 4 — a chars-based proxy; thresholds are derived defaults, operator-tunable; NEVER billing truth and never promoted to a higher tier)\n'; \
140	    printf 'label\telapsed_s\tEXACT (derived at read time: receipt issued_at vs now; never stored)\n'; \
141	    printf 'label\ttokens\tunavailable_live in interactive sessions (tier UNAVAILABLE); close-time reconciliation via telemetry where headless (tier CLOSE-TIME); never presented at a higher tier\n'; \
142	    printf 'label\tcost_usd\tunavailable_live in interactive sessions (tier UNAVAILABLE); close-time reconciliation via telemetry where headless (tier CLOSE-TIME); never presented at a higher tier\n'; \
143	    } > "$1" ) 2>/dev/null || true
144	}
145	
146	staterow(){ # <receipt-path> <kind> <detail>
147	  local sf
148	  sf="$SDIR/$(basename "$1" .md).tsv"
149	  mkdir -p "$SDIR" 2>/dev/null || return 1
150	  [ -f "$sf" ] || write_labels "$sf" "$(basename "$1")"
151	  printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$(now)" "$2" "$3" >> "$sf"
152	}
153	
154	fval(){ # <file> <field>
155	  awk -v k="$2" 'index($0, k": ")==1 { print substr($0, length(k)+3); exit }' "$1"
156	}
157	is_num(){ printf '%s' "$1" | grep -qE '^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$'; }
158	
159	# The open receipt: among build-os/packets/routing/*.md with executed_mode '-',
160	# the newest by the trailing UTC stamp in the file name (route-task.sh's own
161	# naming), falling back to mtime order for foreign names.
162	open_receipt(){
163	  local f best="" bestkey=""
164	  [ -d "$RDIR" ] || return 1
165	  while IFS= read -r f; do
166	    [ -n "$f" ] || continue
167	    [ "$(fval "$f" executed_mode)" = "-" ] || continue
168	    key="$(basename "$f" .md | grep -oE '[0-9]{8}T[0-9]{6}Z$' || true)"
169	    [ -n "$key" ] || key="0-$(stat -c %Y "$f" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
170	    if [ -z "$best" ] || [ "$key" \> "$bestkey" ]; then best="$f"; bestkey="$key"; fi
171	  done < <(find "$RDIR" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.md' 2>/dev/null | sort)
172	  [ -n "$best" ] && printf '%s' "$best"
173	}
174	
175	count_kind(){ # <receipt-path> <kind> — derived, never stored
176	  local sf
177	  sf="$SDIR/$(basename "$1" .md).tsv"
178	  [ -f "$sf" ] || { echo 0; return; }
179	  awk -F'\t' -v k="$2" '$2==k{n++} END{print n+0}' "$sf"
180	}
181	
182	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- gate -------
183	# Prints a decision protocol on stdout: first line ALLOW or BLOCK, message
184	# after. The wrapper turns BLOCK into exit 2 + stderr; anything malformed —
185	# including this function crashing — FAILS OPEN.
186	gate_decide(){ # <stdin-json>
187	  local in="$1" sub rec mode esc esc_ev deg bud allow ntask nproc kind
188	  command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
189	  sub="$(printf '%s' "$in" | jq -r '.tool_input.subagent_type // "-"' 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
190	  [ -n "$sub" ] || sub="-"
191	  rec="$(open_receipt)" || rec=""
192	  if [ -z "$rec" ]; then
193	    logrow "none" "-" "BLOCK-NO-RECEIPT" "subagent_type=$sub"
194	    printf 'BLOCK\n'
195	    printf 'routing-gate: DISPATCH BLOCKED — no OPEN routing receipt exists under build-os/packets/routing/ (open = executed_mode "-"). A substantive task cannot execute unrouted: issue a routing receipt first via build-os/tools/route-task.sh --task-id <id> --description <text> --descriptor <13-field-json>, then dispatch again. Continue the task — only this unrouted dispatch is refused, not the work.\n'
196	    return 0
197	  fi
198	  mode="$(fval "$rec" selected_mode)"
199	  esc="$(fval "$rec" escalation)"; esc_ev="$(fval "$rec" escalation_evidence)"
200	  deg="$(fval "$rec" degradation_note)"
201	  local task_id; task_id="$(fval "$rec" task_id)"; [ -n "$task_id" ] || task_id="-"
202	
203	  # Dispatch class: process roles are governance ceremony, counted against the
204	  # allowance and attributed governance_process; everything else is task work.
205	  kind="task"
206	  local r; for r in $PROCESS_ROLES; do [ "$sub" = "$r" ] && kind="process"; done
207	
208	  # Effective depth: a filled degradation_note means the receipt has already
209	  # been downgraded to gravito_light — the degradation is binding. An
210	  # evidence-bearing escalation record lifts direct/light to full (escalation
211	  # is legal; silence is not — evidence required, exactly as routing-check.sh).
212	  local eff="$mode" escalated=0
213	  if [ -n "$deg" ] && [ "$deg" != "-" ]; then
214	    eff="gravito_light_degraded"
215	  elif [ "$mode" != "gravito_full" ] && [ "$esc" != "-" ] && [ -n "$esc" ] && [ "$esc_ev" != "-" ] && [ -n "$esc_ev" ]; then
216	    eff="gravito_full"; escalated=1
217	  fi
218	
219	  case "$eff" in
220	    gravito_full) : ;;
221	    gravito_light_degraded)
222	      logrow "$task_id" "$mode" "BLOCK-DEGRADED" "subagent_type=$sub"
223	      printf 'BLOCK\n'
224	      printf 'routing-gate: DISPATCH BLOCKED — receipt %s is DEGRADED to gravito_light (degradation_note is filled), so new dispatch is ceremony above the degraded depth. Consolidate the remaining work into the parent loop, preserve completed subagent outputs, and continue the task in gravito_light. Stop the expensive mode, not the task — do not stop working.\n' "$(basename "$rec")"
225	      return 0 ;;
226	    direct|gravito_light)
227	      logrow "$task_id" "$mode" "BLOCK-MODE-$mode" "subagent_type=$sub"
228	      printf 'BLOCK\n'
229	      printf 'routing-gate: DISPATCH BLOCKED — the open routing receipt %s records %s, and subagent dispatch is ceremony above that depth: executing above the recorded mode with no evidence-bearing escalation record is silent escalation (the executed T5 defect), refused here BEFORE execution rather than at close. Either continue the task in the parent loop at %s, or record a new evidence-bearing escalation decision in the receipt (fill escalation AND escalation_evidence, naming what changed) and dispatch again. Continue the task — only the dispatch is refused, not the work.\n' "$(basename "$rec")" "$mode" "$mode"
230	      return 0 ;;
231	    *) return 1 ;;  # unreadable mode -> fail open in the wrapper
232	  esac
233	
234	  if [ "$kind" = "process" ]; then
235	    allow="$(fval "$rec" process_dispatch_allowance)"
236	    is_num "$allow" || allow="$DEFAULT_PROCESS_ALLOWANCE"
237	    nproc="$(count_kind "$rec" process_dispatch)"
238	    if [ "$nproc" -ge "$allow" ]; then
239	      logrow "$task_id" "$mode" "BLOCK-PROCESS-ALLOWANCE" "subagent_type=$sub n=$nproc allowance=$allow"
240	      printf 'BLOCK\n'
241	      printf 'routing-gate: DISPATCH BLOCKED — process-role dispatches are at the allowance (%s of %s, receipt %s; this dispatch is subagent_type %s, attributed governance_process). The gate chain is governance ceremony with its own budget, separate from task work. Consolidate remaining gate work into the parent loop, preserve completed outputs, and continue the task. Stop the expensive mode, not the task — do not stop working.\n' "$nproc" "$allow" "$(basename "$rec")" "$sub"
242	      return 0
243	    fi
244	    staterow "$rec" process_dispatch "subagent_type=$sub attributed=governance_process" || return 1
245	    logrow "$task_id" "$mode" "ALLOW-PROCESS-DISPATCH" "subagent_type=$sub n=$((nproc+1)) allowance=$allow"
246	    printf 'ALLOW\n'
247	    return 0
248	  fi
249	
250	  # Task dispatch against budget_max_subagents. An escalated receipt carries
251	  # its pre-escalation budget (0 for direct/light), so the Full derived default
252	  # (3) governs where the recorded budget is below it — otherwise an escalation
253	  # would be granted and immediately unusable.
254	  bud="$(fval "$rec" budget_max_subagents)"
255	  is_num "$bud" || bud=0
256	  if [ "$escalated" = "1" ] && [ "$bud" -lt 3 ]; then bud=3; fi
257	  ntask="$(count_kind "$rec" task_dispatch)"
258	  if [ "$ntask" -ge "$bud" ]; then
259	    # THE LIVE BRAKE — before close, not at it. Fire-once degradation: stamp
260	    # via record-degradation.sh (which also appends the DEGRADATION state row).
261	    if [ "$deg" = "-" ] && [ -x "$RECDEG" ]; then
262	      bash "$RECDEG" --receipt "$rec" \
263	        --reason "fan-out throttle: task dispatches at budget_max_subagents ($ntask of $bud); stopped spawning" \
264	        --evidence "live state $SDIR/$(basename "$rec" .md).tsv ($ntask completed dispatch rows preserved)" \
265	        >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
266	    fi
267	    logrow "$task_id" "$mode" "BLOCK-FANOUT-BUDGET" "subagent_type=$sub n=$ntask budget=$bud degradation=stamped"
268	    printf 'BLOCK\n'
269	    printf 'routing-gate: DISPATCH BLOCKED — task dispatches are at budget_max_subagents (%s of %s, receipt %s). Stop fan-out now: consolidate the remaining work into the parent loop, preserve completed subagent outputs (they are recorded in the live state), and continue the task in gravito_light. The degradation has been recorded on the receipt, so an honest close passes the budget gate. Stop the expensive mode, not the task — do not stop working.\n' "$ntask" "$bud" "$(basename "$rec")"
270	    return 0
271	  fi
272	  staterow "$rec" task_dispatch "subagent_type=$sub attributed=task_execution" || return 1
273	  # Close-fill tooling for the contribution table: one stub row per admitted
274	  # Full task dispatch, all '-' (admissions to be filled at close, never zeros).
275	  printf 'contribution: %s | - | - | changed_implementation=- | changed_conclusion=- | caught_defect=- | duplicated_work=- | tokens=- | cost=- | time=-\n' "$sub" >> "$rec" 2>/dev/null || true
276	  logrow "$task_id" "$mode" "ALLOW-TASK-DISPATCH" "subagent_type=$sub n=$((ntask+1)) budget=$bud"
277	  printf 'ALLOW\n'
278	  return 0
279	}
280	
281	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- count ------
282	# The always-on observer. Never blocks, never parses with jq (a node/jq spawn
283	# per tool call is exactly the overhead this path must not carry): one sed pull
284	# of tool_name, one grep per receipt to find the open one, one append.
285	# PACKET-0054: chars= is the ESTIMATE token-proxy input (length of everything
286	# after "tool_input" in the raw event — a chars proxy, not a parse); Read/Grep/
287	# Glob get an exploratory_event row beside their tool_event row; and arm_check
288	# arms the repetitive-loop trip the mutgate enforces.
289	count_tool(){ # <stdin-json>
290	  local in="$1" tool rec ti chars
291	  tool="$(printf '%s' "$in" | sed -n 's/.*"tool_name"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
292	  [ -n "$tool" ] || tool="-"
293	  rec="$(open_receipt)" || rec=""
294	  [ -n "$rec" ] || return 0   # no open receipt: nothing to count against, no state invented
295	  ti="${in#*\"tool_input\"}"; chars="${#ti}"
296	  staterow "$rec" tool_event "tool_name=$tool chars=$chars" || return 1
297	  case "$tool" in
298	    Read|Grep|Glob) staterow "$rec" exploratory_event "tool_name=$tool source=read_class" || return 1 ;;
299	  esac
300	  arm_check "$rec" || return 1
301	  return 0
302	}
303	
304	# Arm the reassessment trip when the window since the last boundary row
305	# (reassess_block / reassess_reset) shows a repetitive parent loop. Arming is
306	# once per window; the trip itself fires ONCE, at the next mutation-capable
307	# call (mutgate). Counters are DERIVED by reading rows, never stored.
308	arm_check(){ # <receipt-path>
309	  local sf run sum armed trip="" val="" thr="" tier="" bud esc_s deg_s v
310	  sf="$SDIR/$(basename "$1" .md).tsv"
311	  [ -f "$sf" ] || return 0
312	  read -r run sum armed <<EOF
313	$(awk -F'\t' '
314	    $2=="reassess_block"||$2=="reassess_reset"{run=0;sum=0;last="";armed=0;next}
315	    $2=="reassess_armed"{armed=1;next}
316	    $2=="tool_event"{
317	      t=""; if(match($3,/tool_name=[^ ]*/)) t=substr($3,RSTART+10,RLENGTH-10);
318	      if(t!="" && t==last) run++; else {run=1;last=t};
319	      if(match($3,/chars=[0-9]+/)) sum+=substr($3,RSTART+6,RLENGTH-6)+0 }
320	    END{print run+0, sum+0, armed+0}' "$sf")
321	EOF
322	  [ "$armed" = "1" ] && return 0
323	  if [ "$run" -ge "$SAME_TOOL_MAX" ] 2>/dev/null; then
324	    trip="same_tool"; val="$run"; thr="$SAME_TOOL_MAX"; tier="EXACT"
325	  else
326	    bud="$(fval "$1" budget_max_uncached_tokens)"
327	    if is_num "$bud" && [ "$((sum / 4))" -ge "$((PROXY_MULT * bud))" ]; then
328	      trip="proxy"; val="$((sum / 4))"; thr="$((PROXY_MULT * bud))"; tier="ESTIMATE"
329	    fi
330	  fi
331	  [ -n "$trip" ] || return 0
332	  esc_s="-"; deg_s="-"
333	  v="$(fval "$1" escalation_evidence)"; [ -n "$v" ] && [ "$v" != "-" ] && esc_s="set"
334	  v="$(fval "$1" degradation_note)";    [ -n "$v" ] && [ "$v" != "-" ] && deg_s="set"
335	  staterow "$1" reassess_armed "trip=$trip value=$val threshold=$thr tier=$tier esc=$esc_s deg=$deg_s" || return 1
336	  return 0
337	}

339	# --------------------------------------------------------------- mutgate -----
340	# The UNIVERSAL TASK-ENTRY boundary (PACKET-0054): every mutation-capable tool
341	# call requires an open routing receipt — including parent-only work that never
342	# dispatches. Classification is a NAMED HEURISTIC (stated in
343	# routing_contract_live.md): a hostile command evades the mutation class with
344	# sh -c or a wrapper; this gate is discipline-for-honest-agents plus an audit
345	# trail, NOT a sandbox — the sandbox is the platform's permission system.
346	#
347	# THE STRUCTURED ROUTING ACTION (PACKET-0055). The deadlock-guard exception —
348	# the SOLE ungated pass in the task-entry boundary — no longer substring-
349	# matches the raw event (the operator ruled that breadth "a real enforcement
350	# bypass, not merely a wording issue"). It fires only when the ACTUAL
351	# tool_input.command field, extracted and trimmed, IS exactly one clean
352	# routing-tool invocation: an optional interpreter prefix (bash/sh for the .sh
353	# tools, node for mode-select.mjs), an optional path prefix, exactly one of
354	# route-task.sh | mode-select.mjs | routing-check.sh | record-degradation.sh,
355	# then arguments free of every chaining/substitution metacharacter — no ';',
356	# '&', '|', backtick, '$(', '<', '>', no newline; quotes, braces, brackets,
357	# colons and commas stay legal, so the refusal's own quoted-JSON --descriptor
358	# recovery example passes. Everything that merely MENTIONS a routing tool —
359	# compound commands, comments, sh -c/eval wrappers, substitution, routing-tool
360	# paths in non-command fields — and every event the extractor cannot read
361	# falls THROUGH to normal classification: extraction fails TOWARD GATING,
362	# never toward an ungated pass (the recovery command is clean and always
363	# extracts, so the fall-through cannot re-create the deadlock). The extraction
364	# is itself a heuristic over JSON-in-shell, and that failure direction is its
365	# stated bound.
366	RT_STRICT='^((bash|sh) +)?([A-Za-z0-9._/-]*/)?(route-task\.sh|routing-check\.sh|record-degradation\.sh)( |$)|^(node +)?([A-Za-z0-9._/-]*/)?mode-select\.mjs( |$)'
367	
368	extract_command(){ # <raw-json> -> tool_input.command's JSON string content (escape-encoded); rc 1 = absent/unreadable
369	  local in="$1" rest raw
370	  case "$in" in *'"command"'*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
371	  # First occurrence of the unescaped key: a decoy INSIDE a JSON string value
372	  # is necessarily \"-escaped, so its colon-quote shape cannot match below.
373	  rest="${in#*\"command\"}"
374	  raw="$(printf '%s' "$rest" | sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\(\([^"\\]\|\\.\)*\)".*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
375	  [ -n "$raw" ] || return 1
376	  printf '%s' "$raw"
377	}
378	
379	routing_action(){ # <raw-json> -> "<tool>\t<decoded command>" iff the command IS one clean routing invocation; rc 1 otherwise
380	  local in="$1" raw cmd stripped t BS='\' SENT=$'\x01'
381	  raw="$(extract_command "$in")" || return 1
382	  # Only the benign JSON escapes \" \\ \/ may appear: any other escape (\n,
383	  # \t, \u003b, ...) could conceal a metacharacter from the checks below, so
384	  # its presence falls through — toward gating.
385	  stripped="$(printf '%s' "$raw" | sed 's|\\["\\/]||g')"
386	  case "$stripped" in *"$BS"*) return 1 ;; esac
387	  # Decode the three benign escapes so the checks and the fingerprint see the
388	  # command exactly as the shell receives it. Decoding cannot conceal a
389	  # forbidden character: none of the three decodes to one.
390	  cmd=${raw//"$BS$BS"/$SENT}
391	  cmd=${cmd//"$BS"\"/\"}
392	  cmd=${cmd//"$BS"\//\/}
393	  cmd=${cmd//$SENT/$BS}
394	  cmd="${cmd#"${cmd%%[! ]*}"}"; cmd="${cmd%"${cmd##*[! ]}"}"
395	  [ -n "$cmd" ] || return 1
396	  case "$cmd" in
397	    *';'*|*'&'*|*'|'*|*'`'*|*'$('*|*'<'*|*'>'*|*$'\n'*|*$'\t'*|*$'\r'*) return 1 ;;
398	  esac
399	  printf '%s' "$cmd" | grep -qE "$RT_STRICT" || return 1
400	  t="$(printf '%s' "$cmd" | grep -oE 'route-task\.sh|mode-select\.mjs|routing-check\.sh|record-degradation\.sh' | head -n1)"
401	  printf '%s\t%s' "$t" "$cmd"
402	}

404	# Can the receipt store be used at all — listable where it exists, creatable
405	# where it is not? When NEITHER holds, route-task.sh could never write the
406	# receipt a block would demand, so mutgate_decide FAILS OPEN instead of
407	# refusing into a dead end (PACKET-0055; the trace rides the stderr fallback).
408	store_available(){
409	  if [ -d "$RDIR" ]; then ls "$RDIR" >/dev/null 2>&1; else mkdir -p "$RDIR" 2>/dev/null; fi
410	}

412	# --- BOOTSTRAP CHANNEL (authority_bootstrap_permission_class_mismatch) -------
413	#
414	# EXP-0005 measured every Gravito arm producing zero mutations. Reproduction
415	# refuted the recorded cause: the gate ALLOWS route-task.sh and route-task.sh
416	# works on a clean clone. What failed was one layer out — the HOST permission
417	# layer refused the Bash invocation in headless sessions with no approver.
418	#
419	# The defect is a PERMISSION-CLASS MISMATCH: earning first authority required
420	# Bash (frequently approval-gated) even when the authorized work needed only
421	# Edit/Write (auto-approved). Native paid host denials as friction because its
422	# work path was Edit; Gravito paid one as total paralysis because Edit itself
423	# was gated behind that Bash call.
424	#
425	# THE INVARIANT: first mutation authority must not depend on an operation class
426	# whose host permission requirements are stricter than the mutation class it
427	# authorizes.
428	#
429	# THE CHANNEL: a routing request may be expressed by WRITING one file. Writes
430	# to that exact path — and no other — are ungated, because the path is the
431	# routing channel, not product mutation. Writing it authorizes NOTHING by
432	# itself: the request is schema-checked and then routed through the ordinary
433	# route-task.sh, so the descriptor, the mode selection and every downstream
434	# budget/escalation/close rule apply unchanged.
435	REQ_FILE="$RDIR/routing-request.json"
436	
437	extract_file_path(){ # <raw-json> -> tool_input.file_path; rc 1 = absent
438	  local in="$1" rest raw
439	  case "$in" in *'"file_path"'*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
440	  rest="${in#*\"file_path\"}"
441	  raw="$(printf '%s' "$rest" | sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\(\([^"\\]\|\\.\)*\)".*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
442	  [ -n "$raw" ] || return 1
443	  printf '%s' "$raw"
444	}
445	
446	is_routing_request_path(){ # <raw-json> -> rc 0 iff the write targets exactly the request file
447	  local fp; fp="$(extract_file_path "$1")" || return 1
448	  case "$fp" in
449	    */build-os/packets/routing/routing-request.json|build-os/packets/routing/routing-request.json) return 0 ;;
450	    *) return 1 ;;
451	  esac
452	}
453	
454	mut_classify(){ # <raw-json> <tool> -> routing_tool | git_readonly | mutation | other
455	  local in="$1" tool="$2"
456	  case "$tool" in
457	    Edit|Write|NotebookEdit)
458	      # The routing channel itself is not product mutation. Exactly one path.
459	      if is_routing_request_path "$in"; then printf 'routing_request'; return 0; fi
460	      printf 'mutation'; return 0 ;;
461	    Bash) : ;;
462	    *) printf 'other'; return 0 ;;
463	  esac
464	  # DEADLOCK GUARD, structured (PACKET-0055): exactly-recognized routing
465	  # invocations only — without an ungated pass here no session could issue the
466	  # receipt its first gated call requires; anything short of an exact
467	  # invocation falls through to the git/mutation classes and gates.
468	  if routing_action "$in" >/dev/null; then printf 'routing_tool'; return 0; fi
469	  if printf '%s' "$in" | grep -qE '(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])git([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)'; then
470	    # Any git command carrying a mutating subcommand or a force flag is
471	    # mutation-capable — checked FIRST so `git status && git push` gates.
472	    if printf '%s' "$in" | grep -qE '(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_-])(push|commit|merge|rebase|reset|checkout|restore|clean|apply|am|cherry-pick|tag|stash)([^A-Za-z0-9_-]|$)|--force(-with-lease)?([^A-Za-z0-9_-]|$)|[[:space:]]-f([[:space:]\"\\]|$)'; then
473	      printf 'mutation'; return 0
474	    fi
475	    # The read-only inspection class, by git subcommand. `git -C dir status`
476	    # and other indirections fall through to mutation-capable — conservative.
477	    if printf '%s' "$in" | grep -qE 'git[[:space:]]+(status|log|diff|show|rev-parse|ls-files|branch)([^A-Za-z0-9_-]|$)'; then
478	      printf 'git_readonly'; return 0
479	    fi
480	    printf 'mutation'; return 0
481	  fi
482	  printf 'mutation'   # Bash defaults to mutation-capable: the boundary is entry, not tool trivia
483	}

485	# Route a pending request through the ordinary tool. Returns 0 only when a
486	# receipt was actually minted. Deterministic, idempotent (the request is
487	# consumed), and audited with the request's sha256.
488	redeem_routing_request(){
489	  [ -f "$REQ_FILE" ] || return 1
490	  command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1 || { logrow "none" "-" "BOOTSTRAP-REQUEST-REFUSED" "reason=node-unavailable"; return 1; }
491	
492	  local tid desc descr sha rt out
493	  # Schema check: task_id, description and a descriptor object must all be
494	  # present. Anything missing is a refusal, never a permissive default.
495	  if ! node -e '
496	    const fs=require("fs");
497	    const j=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(process.argv[1],"utf8"));
498	    if(!j.task_id||!j.description||!j.descriptor||typeof j.descriptor!=="object") process.exit(1);
499	    if(!/^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$/.test(j.task_id)) process.exit(1);
500	  ' "$REQ_FILE" 2>/dev/null; then
501	    sha="$(sha256sum "$REQ_FILE" 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-12)"
502	    logrow "none" "-" "BOOTSTRAP-REQUEST-REFUSED" "reason=schema-invalid sha256=${sha:--}"
503	    rm -f "$REQ_FILE"
504	    return 1
505	  fi
506	
507	  tid="$(node -e 'console.log(JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(process.argv[1],"utf8")).task_id)' "$REQ_FILE" 2>/dev/null)"
508	  desc="$(node -e 'console.log(JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(process.argv[1],"utf8")).description)' "$REQ_FILE" 2>/dev/null)"
509	  descr="$(node -e 'console.log(JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(process.argv[1],"utf8")).descriptor))' "$REQ_FILE" 2>/dev/null)"
510	  sha="$(sha256sum "$REQ_FILE" 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-12)"
511	  rt="$DATA_ROOT/build-os/tools/route-task.sh"
512	  [ -x "$rt" ] || [ -f "$rt" ] || { logrow "none" "-" "BOOTSTRAP-REQUEST-REFUSED" "reason=route-task-missing"; return 1; }
513	
514	  # Consume FIRST, so a failing route cannot be retried in a loop.
515	  rm -f "$REQ_FILE"
516	  out="$(bash "$rt" --task-id "$tid" --description "$desc" --descriptor "$descr" 2>&1)" || {
517	    logrow "none" "-" "BOOTSTRAP-REQUEST-REFUSED" "reason=route-task-failed sha256=${sha:--} detail=$(printf '%s' "$out" | tr -d '\t\r\n' | cut -c1-120)"
518	    return 1
519	  }
520	  logrow "$tid" "-" "BOOTSTRAP-RECEIPT-MINTED" "via=routing-request-channel sha256=${sha:--} task_id=$tid"
521	  return 0
522	}

524	mutgate_decide(){ # <stdin-json> — protocol on stdout: ALLOW or BLOCK + message
525	  local in="$1" tool cls rec tid="none" mode="-" v act rtool rcmd sha exc
526	  tool="$(printf '%s' "$in" | sed -n 's/.*"tool_name"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
527	  [ -n "$tool" ] || return 1   # unreadable event -> fail open in the wrapper
528	  cls="$(mut_classify "$in" "$tool")"
529	  rec="$(open_receipt)" || rec=""
530	  if [ -n "$rec" ]; then tid="$(fval "$rec" task_id)"; mode="$(fval "$rec" selected_mode)"; [ -n "$tid" ] || tid="-"; fi
531	  case "$cls" in
532	    routing_tool)
533	      # THE ACTION FINGERPRINT (PACKET-0055): the pass row records WHICH tool
534	      # matched, the first 12 hex chars of the exact command's sha256, and a
535	      # sanitized <=80-char excerpt (tabs/newlines stripped — the ledgers are
536	      # TSV). Only exact invocations reach this label at all, so the ledger
537	      # alone now distinguishes "ran route-task.sh" from anything else.
538	      act="$(routing_action "$in")" || act=$'-\t-'
539	      rtool="${act%%$'\t'*}"; rcmd="${act#*$'\t'}"
540	      sha="-"
541	      if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
542	        sha="$(printf '%s' "$rcmd" | sha256sum 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-12)"; [ -n "$sha" ] || sha="-"
543	      fi
544	      exc="$(printf '%s' "$rcmd" | tr -d '\t\r\n' | cut -c1-80)"
545	      logrow "$tid" "$mode" "ROUTING-TOOL-PASS" "tool=$tool ungated=deadlock-guard routing_tool=$rtool sha256=$sha cmd=$exc"
546	      [ -n "$rec" ] && { staterow "$rec" routing_tool_pass "tool_name=$tool routing_tool=$rtool sha256=$sha cmd=$exc" || true; }
547	      printf 'ALLOW\n'; return 0 ;;
548	    git_readonly)
549	      logrow "$tid" "$mode" "GIT-READONLY-PASS" "tool=$tool class=exploratory heuristic=git-subcommand"
550	      [ -n "$rec" ] && { staterow "$rec" exploratory_event "tool_name=$tool source=git_readonly" || true; }
551	      printf 'ALLOW\n'; return 0 ;;
552	    routing_request)
553	      # Writing the request authorizes NOTHING. It is allowed because the path
554	      # is the routing channel, and it is logged so the ledger shows the
555	      # request separately from the receipt it may later mint.
556	      logrow "$tid" "$mode" "ROUTING-REQUEST-WRITE" "tool=$tool ungated=bootstrap-channel path=routing-request.json"
557	      printf 'ALLOW\n'; return 0 ;;
558	    other)
559	      printf 'ALLOW\n'; return 0 ;;
560	  esac
561	  if [ -z "$rec" ]; then
562	    # BOOTSTRAP REDEMPTION. A pending, schema-valid request is routed through
563	    # the ordinary route-task.sh — from inside the hook, which executes outside
564	    # the tool-permission layer. That is the whole fix: the worker earned
565	    # authority using the SAME permission class as the work it authorizes.
566	    # A malformed request mints nothing and the block below stands.
567	    if redeem_routing_request; then
568	      rec="$(open_receipt)" || rec=""
569	      if [ -n "$rec" ]; then
570	        tid="$(fval "$rec" task_id)"; mode="$(fval "$rec" selected_mode)"
571	        printf 'ALLOW\n'; return 0
572	      fi
573	    fi
574	  fi
575	  if [ -z "$rec" ]; then
576	    if ! store_available; then
577	      # STORE-UNAVAILABLE IS NOT A BRICK (PACKET-0055): with the store neither
578	      # readable nor creatable, route-task.sh could never write the receipt a
579	      # block would demand — a refusal here is a dead end whose own recovery
580	      # command cannot succeed. FAIL OPEN instead, traced: the row itself
581	      # rides the stderr fallback (UNLOGGED(store unwritable)) whenever the
582	      # log file shares the store's fate — the layer-4 mechanics of 0053.
583	      logrow "none" "-" "FAIL-OPEN-STORE-UNAVAILABLE" "tool=$tool store unreadable and uncreatable: recovery cannot succeed, so blocking would be a dead end"
584	      printf 'ALLOW\n'
585	      return 0
586	    fi
587	    logrow "none" "-" "BLOCK-MUTATION-NO-RECEIPT" "tool=$tool"
588	    printf 'BLOCK\n'
589	    # THE REFUSAL IS GENERATED BY THE SELECTOR, not hand-authored here. One
590	    # ruleset decides both what self-audit calls incompatible and what the
591	    # worker is told to do, so the advertised recovery cannot drift away from
592	    # the path that actually works on this host. A static message that says
593	    # "run this Bash command" while the host denies Bash is how EXP-0005
594	    # produced 0/12.
595	    # CODE_ROOT, not DATA_ROOT. The recovery generator is CODE that ships with
596	    # this gate, not per-repo DATA. Resolving it under the data root meant that
597	    # whenever the two differ -- which is the entire purpose of
598	    # ROUTING_GATE_ROOT / CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR -- the selector silently could not
599	    # be found, and the gate fell through to the fallback that advertises the
600	    # shell route unconditionally. That is precisely the behaviour the selector
601	    # was made load-bearing to prevent, reappearing in the one configuration
602	    # nobody ran. The same call already resolves --gate under CODE_ROOT.
603	    _rec="$CODE_ROOT/build-os/assumptions/gate-recovery.mjs"
604	    if command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -f "$_rec" ] \
605	       && node "$_rec" --tool "$tool" --gate "$CODE_ROOT/.claude/hooks/routing-gate.sh" 2>/dev/null; then
606	      logrow "$tid" "-" "RECOVERY-SELECTED" "tool=$tool host=${GRAVITO_HOST_PROFILE:-unknown_conservative} source=selector"
607	    else
608	      # Fail toward DISCOVERABILITY: with no selector, advertise every route
609	      # rather than none, lowest privilege first. A worker told nothing cannot
610	      # proceed; a worker told too much merely spends one extra call.
611	      printf 'routing-gate: MUTATION BLOCKED — %s is mutation-capable and NO OPEN routing receipt exists under build-os/packets/routing/.\n' "$tool"
612	      printf 'SELECTOR UNAVAILABLE — every known recovery is listed, lowest privilege first:\n'
613	      printf 'RECOVERY A — no shell required. WRITE build-os/packets/routing/routing-request.json with {"task_id":"<id>","description":"<one line>","descriptor":{...13 fields...}}, then retry.\n'
614	      printf 'RECOVERY B — via shell: build-os/tools/route-task.sh --task-id <id> --description "<one line>" --descriptor <13-field-json>\n'
615	      printf 'Continue the task — only this unrouted call is refused, not the work.\n'
616	      logrow "$tid" "-" "RECOVERY-FALLBACK" "tool=$tool reason=selector-unavailable"
617	    fi
618	    return 0
619	  fi
620	  # The fire-once REASSESS trip: armed by the counter, enforced here, reset by
621	  # a reassessment record (fresh receipt = fresh state file; or an escalation/
622	  # degradation entry landing after the arming snapshot).
623	  local sf armed esc_s deg_s snap_esc snap_deg
624	  sf="$SDIR/$(basename "$rec" .md).tsv"
625	  armed=""
626	  if [ -f "$sf" ]; then
627	    armed="$(awk -F'\t' '$2=="reassess_block"||$2=="reassess_reset"{a=""} $2=="reassess_armed"{a=$3} END{print a}' "$sf")"
628	  fi
629	  if [ -n "$armed" ]; then
630	    esc_s="-"; deg_s="-"
631	    v="$(fval "$rec" escalation_evidence)"; [ -n "$v" ] && [ "$v" != "-" ] && esc_s="set"
632	    v="$(fval "$rec" degradation_note)";    [ -n "$v" ] && [ "$v" != "-" ] && deg_s="set"
633	    snap_esc="$(printf '%s' "$armed" | sed -n 's/.*esc=\([^ ]*\).*/\1/p')"; [ -n "$snap_esc" ] || snap_esc="-"
634	    snap_deg="$(printf '%s' "$armed" | sed -n 's/.*deg=\([^ ]*\).*/\1/p')"; [ -n "$snap_deg" ] || snap_deg="-"
635	    if [ "$esc_s" != "$snap_esc" ] || [ "$deg_s" != "$snap_deg" ]; then
636	      staterow "$rec" reassess_reset "reason=reassessment-record-landed esc=$esc_s deg=$deg_s (armed snapshot esc=$snap_esc deg=$snap_deg)" || true
637	      logrow "$tid" "$mode" "REASSESS-RESET" "tool=$tool $armed"
638	      # fall through to ALLOW — the trip is reset, the counters restart
639	    else
640	      staterow "$rec" reassess_block "$armed fired=once" || true
641	      logrow "$tid" "$mode" "BLOCK-REASSESS" "tool=$tool $armed"
642	      printf 'BLOCK\n'
643	      printf 'routing-gate: MUTATION BLOCKED ONCE — REASSESS. A repetitive parent loop tripped on receipt %s (%s). Where the trip is the token proxy, its value is tier ESTIMATE — chars/4, never billing truth. The thresholds are derived defaults, operator-tunable (ROUTING_REASSESS_SAME_TOOL_MAX, ROUTING_REASSESS_PROXY_MULT). Re-route before continuing: confirm the mode via build-os/tools/route-task.sh (a fresh receipt), or record an evidence-bearing escalation on the receipt, or degrade honestly via build-os/tools/record-degradation.sh. This trip fires exactly once — the next mutation-capable call passes, and a reassessment record resets the trip. Continue the task — only this one call is refused, not the work.\n' "$(basename "$rec")" "$armed"
644	      return 0
645	    fi
646	  fi
647	  staterow "$rec" mutation_event "tool_name=$tool class=mutation" || return 1
648	  logrow "$tid" "$mode" "ALLOW-MUTATION" "tool=$tool"
649	  printf 'ALLOW\n'
650	  return 0
651	}

668	status_report(){
669	  local rec sf issued elapsed
670	  rec="$(open_receipt)" || rec=""
671	  if [ -z "$rec" ]; then printf 'routing-gate: status — no open receipt\n'; return 0; fi
672	  sf="$SDIR/$(basename "$rec" .md).tsv"
673	  printf 'routing-gate: status receipt=%s\n' "$(basename "$rec")"
674	  printf 'selected_mode: %s\n' "$(fval "$rec" selected_mode)"
675	  printf 'task_dispatches: %s (EXACT, derived from %s)\n' "$(count_kind "$rec" task_dispatch)" "${sf#"$DATA_ROOT/"}"
676	  printf 'process_dispatches: %s (EXACT, attributed governance_process)\n' "$(count_kind "$rec" process_dispatch)"
677	  printf 'tool_events: %s (EXACT, sessions where the gate is loaded)\n' "$(count_kind "$rec" tool_event)"
678	  printf 'exploratory_events: %s (EXACT — the explore half of the explore/execute split)\n' "$(count_kind "$rec" exploratory_event)"
679	  printf 'mutation_events: %s (EXACT — admitted mutation-capable calls)\n' "$(count_kind "$rec" mutation_event)"
680	  if [ -f "$sf" ]; then
681	    printf 'token_proxy: %s (ESTIMATE — sum of tool-input chars / 4; never billing truth)\n' \
682	      "$(awk -F'\t' '$2=="tool_event" && match($3,/chars=[0-9]+/){s+=substr($3,RSTART+6,RLENGTH-6)+0} END{print int(s/4)}' "$sf")"
683	  else
684	    printf 'token_proxy: 0 (ESTIMATE — no state rows yet)\n'
685	  fi
686	  printf 'tool_failures: %s (EXACT only where PostToolUse exposes status)\n' "$(count_kind "$rec" tool_failure)"
687	  issued="$(fval "$rec" issued_at)"
688	  if elapsed="$(( $(date -u +%s) - $(date -ud "$issued" +%s 2>/dev/null || echo 0) ))" 2>/dev/null && [ -n "$issued" ]; then
689	    printf 'elapsed_s: %s (EXACT, derived at read time: issued_at %s vs now)\n' "$elapsed" "$issued"
690	  else
691	    printf 'elapsed_s: - (issued_at unreadable)\n'
692	  fi
693	  printf 'tokens: unavailable_live (close-time reconciliation via telemetry where headless)\n'
694	  printf 'cost_usd: unavailable_live (close-time reconciliation via telemetry where headless)\n'
695	  return 0
696	}
697	
698	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- wrapper ----
699	CMD="${1:-}"
700	case "$CMD" in
701	  gate|mutgate|count|post|status) ;;
702	  -h|--help|help) sed -n '2,70p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"; exit 0 ;;
703	  *) printf 'routing-gate: unknown command "%s" — expected gate|mutgate|count|post|status\n' "${CMD:-}" >&2; exit 2 ;;
704	esac
705	
706	if [ "$CMD" = "status" ]; then status_report; exit $?; fi
707	
708	# ALWAYS drain stdin first (the DEFECT-0013 lesson: an undrained producer under
709	# pipefail is a race) — and never let a read failure become a blocked call.
710	IN="$(cat 2>/dev/null || true)"
711	
712	if [ "${ROUTING_GATE_DISABLE:-0}" = "1" ]; then
713	  # OPERATOR-ONLY escape, refused-by-default posture: it exists, it is
714	  # documented in routing_contract_live.md, and it ALWAYS leaves a trace.
715	  logrow "-" "-" "DISABLED-BY-OPERATOR" "cmd=$CMD ROUTING_GATE_DISABLE=1"
716	  exit 0
717	fi
718	
719	case "$CMD" in
720	  count)
721	    count_tool "$IN" || logrow "-" "-" "FAIL-OPEN" "cmd=count internal error"
722	    exit 0 ;;
723	  post)
724	    post_tool "$IN" || logrow "-" "-" "FAIL-OPEN" "cmd=post internal error"
725	    exit 0 ;;
726	  gate|mutgate)
727	    # Keep the hook's REAL stderr reachable on fd 9: the decide functions run
728	    # with stderr silenced (incidental tool noise must not pollute a refusal),
729	    # but logrow's unwritable-store fallback line must still escape — a trace
730	    # that dies inside the capture is no trace (PACKET-0055).
731	    exec 9>&2
732	    if [ "$CMD" = "gate" ]; then
733	      OUT="$(gate_decide "$IN" 2>/dev/null)"; RC=$?
734	    else
735	      OUT="$(mutgate_decide "$IN" 2>/dev/null)"; RC=$?
736	    fi
737	    DECISION="$(printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | sed -n '1p')"
738	    if [ "$RC" -eq 0 ] && [ "$DECISION" = "ALLOW" ]; then
739	      exit 0
740	    elif [ "$RC" -eq 0 ] && [ "$DECISION" = "BLOCK" ]; then
741	      printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | sed '1d' >&2
742	      exit 2
743	    else
744	      # FAIL OPEN: a broken gate must not brick every session. Logged, because
745	      # a silent fail-open is an invisible outage of the control plane.
746	      logrow "-" "-" "FAIL-OPEN" "cmd=$CMD rc=$RC decision=${DECISION:-none}"
747	      exit 0
748	    fi ;;
749	esac
750	exit 0
751
